question: Three partners A, B, and C started a business. A invested Rs. 30,000, B invested Rs. 20,000, and C invested Rs. 25,000. After 6 months, A withdrew Rs. 5,000 and C invested Rs. 7,000 more. At the end of the year, the firm incurred a loss of Rs. 24,000. Find the share of loss borne by partner C.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Rs. 9,000.

GIVEN

• A: Rs. 30,000 for 6 months then Rs. 25,000; B: Rs. 20,000 for 12 months; C: Rs. 25,000 for 6 months then Rs. 32,000. Total loss = Rs. 24,000.

SOLUTION

• Capital × time (in thousands): A = 30×6 + 25×6 = 330; B = 20×12 = 240; C = 25×6 + 32×6 = 342.

• Ratio A : B : C = 330 : 240 : 342. Total = 912.

• C's loss = 24,000 × 342/912 = 24,000 × 0.375 = Rs. 9,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Divide the ratio by 6: 55 : 40 : 57, total 152. C's share = 24000 × 57/152 = 9,000 directly.

NOTE

• In partnership, profit/loss is shared in the ratio of (capital × time). Handle mid-year changes by splitting into equal time blocks.

question: A tank contains 120 litres of liquid, 30% of which is alcohol. If 30 litres of this mixture is replaced by another liquid containing 50% alcohol, what is the percentage of alcohol in the resulting solution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 35%.

GIVEN

• 120 L liquid, 30% alcohol. Remove 30 L of mixture, add 30 L of 50% alcohol.

SOLUTION

• Initial alcohol = 30% of 120 = 36 L.

• Removing 30 L of mixture removes 30% × 30 = 9 L alcohol → 27 L alcohol left in 90 L.

• Adding 30 L of 50% alcohol adds 15 L → alcohol = 27 + 15 = 42 L in 120 L.

• Percentage = 42/120 × 100 = 35%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only 1/4 of the tank changes. New % = 30% × 3/4 + 50% × 1/4 = 22.5 + 12.5 = 35%.

NOTE

• In replacement problems, the final concentration is the weighted average of the retained and added portions.

question: The ratio of the speeds of two trains is 5:7. If the faster train travels 210 km in 3 hours, find the time taken by the slower train to cover 150 km.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3 hours.

GIVEN

• Speed ratio (slower : faster) = 5 : 7. Faster train: 210 km in 3 hours.

SOLUTION

• Faster speed = 210 ÷ 3 = 70 km/h → this is 7 parts, so 1 part = 10 km/h.

• Slower speed = 5 parts = 50 km/h.

• Time for 150 km = 150 ÷ 50 = 3 hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Slower speed = 70 × 5/7 = 50 km/h; time = 150/50 = 3 h in one line.

NOTE

• Speed = Distance ÷ Time. When speeds are in a ratio, scale one known value to find the unit part.

question: Arrange the following values in ascending order.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2 3/8 < 2 1/2 < 37/14 < 20/7.

GIVEN

• Values: 2 3/8, 20/7, 2 1/2, 37/14.

SOLUTION

• Convert to decimals: 2 3/8 = 2.375; 20/7 ≈ 2.857; 2 1/2 = 2.5; 37/14 ≈ 2.643.

• Ascending: 2.375 < 2.5 < 2.643 < 2.857.

• So order = 2 3/8 < 2 1/2 < 37/14 < 20/7.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• All values are between 2 and 3; compare only the fractional parts (0.375, 0.857, 0.5, 0.643) to rank quickly.

NOTE

• Converting mixed numbers and improper fractions to decimals is the fastest reliable way to order them.

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 16/57.

GIVEN

• Expression: 1/(8+√7) + 1/(8−√7).

SOLUTION

• Common denominator: (8+√7)(8−√7) = 8² − (√7)² = 64 − 7 = 57.

• Numerator: (8−√7) + (8+√7) = 16.

• Value = 16/57 = 16/57.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For 1/(a+b) + 1/(a−b), answer is directly 2a/(a²−b²) = 16/57.

NOTE

• Use the identity (a+b)(a−b) = a² − b² to rationalise sums of conjugate fractions instantly.

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 7√10/30.

GIVEN

• [(√5+√2)² + (√5−√2)²] ÷ 6√10.

SOLUTION

• (√5+√2)² = 7 + 2√10 and (√5−√2)² = 7 − 2√10.

• Sum = 14.

• 14/(6√10) = 7/(3√10) = 7√10/30 (rationalising) = 7√10/30.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Use (a+b)² + (a−b)² = 2(a² + b²) = 2(5 + 2) = 14; then divide by 6√10.

NOTE

• (a+b)² + (a−b)² = 2(a² + b²) removes cross terms instantly — a key surd shortcut.

question: What is the remainder when 1349 is divided by 8?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5.

GIVEN

• Find remainder of 1349 ÷ 8.

SOLUTION

• 8 × 168 = 1344.

• 1349 − 1344 = 5.

• Remainder = 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For divisibility by 8, only the last 3 digits matter: 349 ÷ 8 = 43 remainder 5.

NOTE

• A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a multiple of 8; else that gives the remainder.

question: Which of the following number is neither divisible by 9 nor by 11?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3472.

GIVEN

• Options: 3472, 3168, 3366, 3465.

SOLUTION

• 3472: digit sum = 3+4+7+2 = 16 (not divisible by 9); alternating sum = 3−4+7−2 = 4 (not divisible by 11). So neither.

• 3168: sum 18 (÷9). 3366: alt sum 0 (÷11). 3465: sum 18 (÷9).

• Hence 3472 is neither divisible by 9 nor 11.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Div by 9 → digit sum multiple of 9; div by 11 → alternating digit sum multiple of 11. Screen all four fast.

NOTE

• 11 rule: (sum of odd-position digits) − (sum of even-position digits) must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

question: The average of 10 numbers is X and one of these numbers is 70. If 70 is replaced with 30, then what will be the new average?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. X − 4.

GIVEN

• Average of 10 numbers = X; 70 is replaced by 30.

SOLUTION

• Change in total = 30 − 70 = −40.

• Change in average = −40 ÷ 10 = −4.

• New average = X − 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• New average = old average + (change in value)/(count) = X + (−40)/10 = X − 4.

NOTE

• Replacing one value shifts the average by (difference of values) ÷ (number of terms).

question: 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + …… + 45³ = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1071225.

GIVEN

• Sum of cubes 1³ + 2³ + … + 45³.

SOLUTION

• Formula: [n(n+1)/2]² with n = 45.

• n(n+1)/2 = 45 × 46 / 2 = 1035.

• Sum = 1035² = 1071225.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Sum of cubes = (sum of first n natural numbers)². Just square 1035.

NOTE

• 1³ + 2³ + … + n³ = [n(n+1)/2]² — the square of the triangular number.

question: The average of 12 numbers is 46. Four numbers 20, 8, 12 and 40 were removed. What will be the new average?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 59.

GIVEN

• Average of 12 numbers = 46. Remove 20, 8, 12, 40.

SOLUTION

• Total of 12 numbers = 12 × 46 = 552.

• Sum removed = 20 + 8 + 12 + 40 = 80.

• Remaining 8 numbers sum = 552 − 80 = 472; new average = 472 ÷ 8 = 59.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Removed 4 numbers average 20; they pull the mean up because 20 < 46. New avg = (552 − 80)/8 = 59.

NOTE

• Average = Sum ÷ Count. Track total sum when items are added or removed.

question: B = 3560 − A. When B is divided by 8, 12 and 16 the remainder is 4 in each case. What is the value of A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• B = 3560 − A; B leaves remainder 4 on division by 8, 12 and 16.

SOLUTION

• LCM(8, 12, 16) = 48, so B = 48k + 4.

• Largest such B not exceeding 3560: 48 × 74 = 3552, so B = 3552 + 4 = 3556.

• A = 3560 − 3556 = 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• (3560 − 4) = 3556; nearest multiple of 48 below it is 3552, giving A = 3556 − 3552 = 4.

NOTE

• A number leaving the same remainder r for several divisors has the form LCM(divisors) × k + r.

question: There is a rectangular floor of size 540 cm × 720 cm. The floor is to tiled with largest square tiles. How many such tiles will be required?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 12.

GIVEN

• Rectangular floor 540 cm × 720 cm; use largest possible square tiles.

SOLUTION

• Largest tile side = HCF(540, 720) = 180 cm.

• Tiles along length = 720 ÷ 180 = 4; along breadth = 540 ÷ 180 = 3.

• Total tiles = 4 × 3 = 12.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Number of tiles = (Area of floor) ÷ (side²) = (540 × 720) ÷ 180² = 388800 ÷ 32400 = 12.

NOTE

• Largest square tile side = HCF of the two dimensions; this leaves no gap or cut.

question: 30 percent of a number exceeds 20 percent of the same number by 40. What is the value of the number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 400.

GIVEN

• 30% of a number − 20% of the same number = 40.

SOLUTION

• (30% − 20%) of number = 10% of number = 40.

• Number = 40 ÷ 0.10 = 400.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The 10% gap equals 40, so 100% = 40 × 10 = 400.

NOTE

• When two percentages of the same quantity differ by a value, use the difference of percentages directly.

question: Cost price of an article is Rs. 400. The profit percentage is 30 percent. What is the value of profit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Rs. 120.

GIVEN

• Cost price = Rs. 400; profit = 30%.

SOLUTION

• Profit = 30% of CP = 30/100 × 400.

• = Rs. 120.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 10% of 400 = 40, so 30% = 40 × 3 = 120.

NOTE

• Profit = Profit% × CP; Selling Price = CP × (1 + Profit%/100).

question: Every day a person sells 40 percent of his fruits and 10 percent of the remaining fruits get spoilt during the night. If total 36 fruits got spoil on the first night, then how many fruits did he sell on the first day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 240.

GIVEN

• Sells 40% of fruits; 10% of the remaining spoil at night; spoilt = 36.

SOLUTION

• Let total = N. Remaining after selling = 60% of N = 0.6N.

• Spoilt = 10% of 0.6N = 0.06N = 36 → N = 600.

• Sold on first day = 40% of 600 = 240.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 36 spoilt = 6% of total, so total = 600; sold = 40% = 240.

NOTE

• Apply successive percentages step by step on the running quantity, not on the original each time.

question: R is 33.33 percent more efficient than S. S alone can finish a work in 24 days. In how many days will R alone finish the same work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 18.

GIVEN

• R is 33.33% (= 1/3) more efficient than S; S alone finishes in 24 days.

SOLUTION

• R's efficiency = S × (1 + 1/3) = 4/3 of S.

• Time is inversely proportional to efficiency, so R's time = 24 × 3/4.

• = 18 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 33.33% = 1/3, so efficiency ratio S : R = 3 : 4; time ratio = 4 : 3 → R = 24 × 3/4 = 18.

NOTE

• 33.33% = 1/3, 25% = 1/4, 20% = 1/5 — memorise fraction equivalents to convert efficiency to time fast.

question: Pipes P1 and P2 alone can fill a tank in 5 hours and 10 hours respectively. Pipe P3 alone can empty the same tank in 20 hours. Firstly, both pipes P1 and P2 are opened and after 1 hour pipe P3 is also opened. In how much total time (in hours) tank will be completely filled?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 19/5.

GIVEN

• P1 fills in 5 h, P2 in 10 h, P3 empties in 20 h. P1, P2 open first; P3 opens after 1 h.

SOLUTION

• Take capacity = 20 units. Rates: P1 = 4, P2 = 2, P3 = −1 unit/h.

• First 1 hour (P1+P2): 4 + 2 = 6 units filled; remaining = 14 units.

• With all three: net = 4 + 2 − 1 = 5 units/h → time for 14 = 14/5 h.

• Total = 1 + 14/5 = 19/5 hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Use LCM capacity (20) for whole-number rates; first-hour head start of 6 units leaves 14/5 h more.

NOTE

• For filling/emptying, add rates (inlet +, outlet −); LCM as capacity avoids fractions.

question: Speeds of train P and Q is 65 m/s and 50 m/s. Train P and Q are running in same direction. They cross each other in 50 seconds. What is total length (in metres) of trains P and Q?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 750.

GIVEN

• Speeds 65 m/s and 50 m/s, same direction; cross each other in 50 s.

SOLUTION

• Relative speed (same direction) = 65 − 50 = 15 m/s.

• Total length crossed = relative speed × time = 15 × 50.

• = 750 metres.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Same direction → subtract speeds; length = 15 × 50 = 750 in one step.

NOTE

• When two trains cross each other, distance = sum of their lengths; use relative speed (− for same, + for opposite direction).

question: A car travels at a speed of 80 km/hr and covers a particular distance in 4 hour 30 minutes. How much time (in hours) another car travelling at the speed of 30 km/hr will take to cover the same distance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 12.

GIVEN

• First car: 80 km/hr for 4 h 30 min. Second car: 30 km/hr, same distance.

SOLUTION

• Distance = 80 × 4.5 = 360 km.

• Time for second car = 360 ÷ 30 = 12 hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Distance fixed → time ∝ 1/speed: 4.5 × (80/30) = 4.5 × 8/3 = 12 h.

NOTE

• For a fixed distance, speed and time are inversely proportional: S1 × T1 = S2 × T2.
